title: need to distinguish superclass dc fields that are already mapped vs. ones that arent

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

labels.name: orm - annotated declarative
labels.description: issues with the new annotations-based declarative ORM approach

body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/9211

issue as shown 

```py
import dataclasses
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, Identity, Integer, String, orm
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column


class Base(orm.DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Model(orm.MappedAsDataclass):
    @orm.declared_attr.directive
    @classmethod
    def __tablename__(cls) -> str:
        return cls.__name__.lower()

    @orm.declared_attr.directive
    @classmethod
    def __mapper_args__(cls) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "polymorphic_identity": cls.__name__,
            "polymorphic_on": "polymorphic_type",
        }

    @orm.declared_attr
    @classmethod
    def polymorphic_type(cls) -> Mapped[str]:
        return mapped_column(
            String,
            insert_default=cls.__name__,
            init=False,
        )


class Book(Model, Base):
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        Integer,
        Identity(),
        primary_key=True,
        init=False,
    )


fields = dataclasses.fields(Book)
print(Book, {field.name: f"init={field.init}" for field in fields})


class Novel(Book):
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("book.id"),
        primary_key=True,
        init=False,
    )
    description: Mapped[Optional[str]]

```

the "polymorphic_type" field is getting copied to Novel without actually having any dataclass field, therefore init=True, due to how we grab elements and put them in annotations.

I've tried some various "correct" ways to make this work but have not figured it out yet.  The basic end result we want however can be achieved via the patch below:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/decl_base.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/decl_base.py
index a858f12cb9..3d0aad7ccc 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/decl_base.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/decl_base.py
@@ -1039,6 +1039,19 @@ class _ClassScanMapperConfig(_MapperConfig):
         manager = instrumentation.manager_of_class(self.cls)
         assert manager is not None
 
+        existing_dataclass_fields = getattr(self.cls, "__dataclass_fields__", {})
+
+        def do_our_check(
+            key,
+        ):
+            if key in existing_dataclass_fields:
+                attr = getattr(self.cls, key)
+                if isinstance(attr, InstrumentedAttribute):
+                    return False
+
+            return True
+
+
         field_list = [
             _AttributeOptions._get_arguments_for_make_dataclass(
                 key,
@@ -1060,6 +1073,9 @@ class _ClassScanMapperConfig(_MapperConfig):
                     attr_value,
                     originating_module,
                 ) in self.collected_annotations.items()
+                if do_our_check(
+                    key
+                )
             )
         ]
         annotations = {}
```

so when we do the collect annotations, we need to look at the field and see if this is already mapped in some more legit way, likely not even collect the annotation at all.
